_doc: Third-party per-token endpoints this repository is authorized to reach. Builder Contract §3: such a vendor is not banned, but it is 'not yours to install: they need the owner's explicit authorization first'. That rule was already in force and could not reach the arming, because arming had become a GUI act — one repository secret, no PR, no review. This file moves the decision to where a merge can see it: a client refuses to speak unless its endpoint is listed HERE, so a secret alone can no longer open an outbound path. An absent, unreadable or malformed file authorizes NOTHING, for the same reason the ban-prose pardon list does: failing open would make deleting one file the way to arm every vendor. The same rule now applies one level down, inside an entry: `{endpoint, ruling}` alone has no field for what the vendor is permitted to touch, so an entry with no perimeter authorizes everything — the fail-open the file itself was built to prevent. An entry must therefore be an object carrying `endpoint`, `ruling` (a dated ruling in docs/rules/RULINGS.md naming the endpoint AND its permitted use), `use` (a short description of what the vendor is for, unread by any client — a ledger field for a human), and `paths` (a non-empty list of non-empty glob-pattern strings declaring what it is INTENDED to touch — `paths` absent, empty, non-list or containing a non-string authorizes NOTHING, same as the file absent; write `["**"]` explicitly for 'anywhere', never leave it out to mean the same thing). NOTE what `paths` does not yet do: no client reads it against a target file — that per-request check is future work for whenever the first entry is added. Today it is a required SHAPE on the entry, not an enforced perimeter.
